note:

- Card, fact: The card gives the cell wall only for the fungal cell and lists only the membrane and cytoplasm as shared. rejected.title: Bacterial and fungal cells
card: Bacterial cell
A bacterial cell is very small and has no nucleus. Its genetic material floats loose in the cytoplasm.
Fungal cell
A fungal cell has a nucleus and a cell wall. It has no chloroplasts, so it cannot make its own food as plants do.
Yeast is a fungus that is a single cell. Mushrooms are also fungi, but they are made of many cells.
Both cells have a cell membrane and cytoplasm. The nucleus is the main difference: bacterial cells lack one, and fungal cells have one.
rejected.remember: Bacteria have no nucleus. Fungi have a nucleus but no chloroplasts.

a.q: Which structure do fungal cells have but bacterial cells do not?
a.why: Fungal cells have a nucleus, while bacterial cells have none. A cell membrane and cytoplasm are found in both, and chloroplasts are found in neither, so none of these is the difference.
a.clue: Think about where each cell keeps its genetic material.

b.q: Sam finds tiny living things feeding on old bread. Each is a single cell with a cell wall and a nucleus, but no chloroplasts. What are they most likely to be?
b.why: A single cell with a nucleus and a cell wall, with no chloroplasts, that feeds on bread matches a fungus such as yeast. Bacteria are tempting because they are single cells too, but they have no nucleus. Plants make their own food rather than feeding on bread.
b.clue: Which single cell has a nucleus but cannot make its own food?

a.q: Which structure do fungal cells have but bacterial cells do not?
a.why: Fungal cells have a nucleus, while bacterial cells have none. Chloroplasts are tempting, but fungal cells have no chloroplasts, so they cannot be the difference.
a.clue: Think about where each cell keeps its genetic material.

b.q: Under a microscope, Sam sees a cell with a cell wall and a nucleus, but no chloroplasts. What type of cell is it most likely to be?
b.why: A cell wall with a nucleus and no chloroplasts matches a fungal cell. A plant cell also has a cell wall and a nucleus, but it has chloroplasts, so it is ruled out.
b.clue: Check which cell has a nucleus but no chloroplasts.

problems.detail: Fungal cells have mitochondria and bacterial cells do not, so 'A mitochondrion' is also a correct answer. Point 2 teaches mitochondria, so students may know this. Replace it with a structure both cells share, such as a cell membrane, or one neither has.

Many plant cells, such as onion epidermis and root cells, have a cell wall and a nucleus but no chloroplasts. Onion skin is the classic Year 7 microscope cell, so 'A plant cell' is defensible. Add a detail that rules plants out, such as a single cell growing on bread, or say the cell is a yeast sample.
Why (b) says a plant cell 'has chloroplasts, so it is ruled out'. That is not true of all plant cells, such as root and onion skin cells.

Fungal cell

b.q: Lena looks at a drop of fermenting fruit juice under a microscope. She sees single cells, each with a cell wall and a nucleus but no chloroplasts. What are they most likely to be?
